conviction_note: One real lead, and I could not put a number on it. On the 2026-07-02 call management said they had already received some IEEPA tariff refunds. EDGAR full-text search finds no 'IEEPA' or 'tariff refunds' in any Bassett filing through the Q2 10-Q, so nothing was booked by May 30 and the refund most likely lands in the quarter ended late August. The EPS bar of $0.13 (Sidoti implies about $0.11) shows no sign of including it. The dollar amount is my inference (about $1.5-3.5m pretax, which would be roughly $0.13-0.30 of EPS), and it is a one-off on a company that gives no guidance. Peers that booked refunds rose (HOFT +10% premarket, FLXS +24%), but LESSONS says refund prints split by guidance direction. So I size the name at +1.0, below the +1.3 sum of findings, because the release will label the refund one-time and operating demand is still described as weak.

On GAAP EPS a refund would put the print far above $0.13. No company guidance exists.

findings.finding: Bassett told its 2026-07-02 call it had already received some IEEPA tariff refunds and expected more. No Bassett filing through the Q2 10-Q (period ended 2026-05-30) contains 'IEEPA' or 'tariff refunds' (EDGAR full-text), so the refund most likely lands in fiscal Q3 (June-August). About 20% of wholesale sales are imported case goods and leather from Vietnam, which scales to an estimated $1.5-3.5m pretax (inferred, not disclosed). That is up to about 2x the $0.13 EPS bar on a GAAP basis.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BSET has no prior refund print. Its only EPS beat in the baseline (Q2, $0.24 vs $0.20 with written sales +9.5%) drew +7.66%; the two misses drew -1.27% and -0.31%. Direct peers that booked IEEPA refunds this summer: HOFT +10% premarket on 2026-09-11 ($7.9m of recoveries, https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/hooker-furnishings-stock-climbs-6-on-earnings-beat-tariff-recovery-93CH-4897631) and FLXS +24% on 2026-08-18 ($9.0m refund in gross margin, https://www.tradingkey.com/news/earnings/262113061-tradingkey).
findings.why_not_priced: If the refund were in the bar, Q3 consensus would sit above Q2's $0.24 rather than at $0.13. Sidoti would not have cut FY26 on 2026-09-28 to a level that implies Q3 of about $0.11. And the stock would not be -4% over 20 days and below its 50-day average going into the print. Management gave no amount on the call and nothing has been filed, so no aggregator can carry the number.
findings.independence: Industry-wide timing from CBP and trade-press data: $106.6bn of refunds completed by 2026-08-21 (https://www.ghy.com/trade-compliance/cbp-cape-ieepa-refund-progress/). Peers recognised refunds in their June-August quarters: Hooker $7.9m (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/11/3360201/8255/en/hooker-furnishings-reports-profitable-quarter-and-first-half.html), Flexsteel $9.0m and Ethan Allen $5m. Import share of 20% is from Bassett's 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/10329/000143774925003216/bset20241130_10k.htm). The amount is still inference, and how the company will account for it is open ('work with public accountants').

findings.finding: Q2 written sales rose 9.5% while delivered sales fell 0.7%, because orders were back-end loaded; wholesale orders rose 5.2% and customer deposits rose to $25.6m. Management said the strong retail trend continued into June. That backlog converts in fiscal Q3, against a revenue bar that asks for only +3.4% YoY ($82.8m vs $80.1m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The written-sales line was the driver of the only large reaction on record: +7.66% on 2026-07-01, when written sales rose 9.5% (baseline, and https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/01/3320973/8488/en/Bassett-Reports-Fiscal-Second-Quarter-Results.html). Delivered revenue has missed and beaten by about 0.2-4% over the last four quarters.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The written-sales figure was in the July release and the consensus of +3.4% YoY already assumes some conversion. What is left is small: the revenue bar is disputed ($82.8m vs $84.72m), which caps this finding. Summer data points the same way but is only a proxy: Census August furniture store sales rose 1.9%, the first rise since October 2025, and La-Z-Boy written same-store sales rose 3%.
findings.independence: Census August 2026 furniture store sales +1.9% YoY (https://homenewsnow.com/blog/2026/09/18/furniture-store-sales-rise-1-9-from-august-2025/); La-Z-Boy FQ1 written same-store sales +3% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000057131/000005713126000034/fy27q1pressrelease.htm); Hooker backlog +6.2% YoY. The other side: Hooker said big-ticket demand 'remains weak' and summer promotions were heavy (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/11/hooker-furnishings-hoft-q2-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). This finding shares no document with the first.

outside_window.finding: Management said the mid-July retail price increase of 200-250 bps will show mostly in fiscal Q4, not Q3, which matters for the Q4 margin and the multiple beyond this print.

baseline_tension: No skew, a -4.27% run-up and a stock below its 50-day average say the market is not leaning long, so a positive finding does not collide with the baseline. The baseline is thin (3 prints, median reaction 1.27%), and the refund lesson (refund prints split by guidance direction, on a company that gives none) keeps the size below the +1.3 sum.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs; refund prints split by guidance direction): the tariff-refund finding went from +2.0 to +1.0. Bassett gives no guidance, the release will almost certainly call the refund one-time, and I could state no path to the multiple.
Lesson 5 / 'documents beat inference': the refund's existence is company-stated, but its amount is inferred from the import share, so I kept the reduced size and a wide band of -2 to +5.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the revenue bar disagrees across sources ($82.8m vs $84.72m), so the backlog-conversion finding was capped from +1.0 to +0.3. The EPS bar of $0.13 has two agreeing sources.
Lesson 3 (caveat reaches the number): expected move went from +2.5 to +1.0, below the +1.3 sum, because of the weak-demand commentary from Hooker and the Sidoti cut.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage) kept me from cutting further: this name paid +7.66% for its last EPS beat, and the upper band of +5 on finding 1 stays.
